subject: Biology
title: Human Reproduction
summary: Humans are sexually reproducing and viviparous. Events: gametogenesis, insemination, fertilisation, cleavage, blastocyst formation, implantation, gestation and parturition.

The male system has testes (seminiferous tubules make sperm; Leydig cells make androgens), ducts, accessory glands and the penis. The female system has ovaries, oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and mammary glands.

Spermatogenesis starts at puberty and gives four sperm per primary spermatocyte; oogenesis starts before birth and gives one ovum per primary oocyte. The menstrual cycle (~28 days) is controlled by FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone.

Fertilisation happens in the ampullary region of the oviduct; the blastocyst implants in the endometrium; the placenta supports the foetus and makes hormones. Birth is triggered by the foetal ejection reflex and oxytocin.

formulas.name: Testis structure
formulas.formula: each testis ~250 testicular lobules, each with 1–3 seminiferous tubules;  lined by spermatogonia and Sertoli cells (nourish sperm);  Leydig (interstitial) cells outside tubules secrete androgens

formulas.name: Male duct path
formulas.formula: seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra

formulas.name: Male accessory glands
formulas.formula: paired seminal vesicles + prostate + paired bulbourethral glands → seminal plasma (fructose, Ca²⁺, enzymes); bulbourethral secretion lubricates the penis

formulas.name: Spermatogenesis
formulas.formula: spermatogonium (2n, 46) → primary spermatocyte (2n) → meiosis I → 2 secondary spermatocytes (n, 23) → meiosis II → 4 spermatids (n) → spermiogenesis → sperm;  release = spermiation

formulas.name: Hormonal control (male)
formulas.formula: GnRH → LH acts on Leydig cells (androgens);  FSH acts on Sertoli cells (factors helping spermiogenesis)

formulas.name: Sperm structure
formulas.formula: head (haploid nucleus + acrosome with enzymes for fertilisation) + neck + middle piece (mitochondria — energy) + tail;  ~200–300 million sperm per ejaculate; ≥ 60% normal shape and ≥ 40% vigorous motility needed for normal fertility

formulas.name: Oogenesis
formulas.formula: oogonia form in foetal life → primary oocyte (arrested in prophase I) in primary follicle → at puberty → secondary oocyte (n) + first polar body (Graafian follicle) → ovulation → meiosis II completes only after sperm entry → ovum + second polar body
formulas.note: No new oogonia form after birth; many follicles degenerate, so at puberty only about 60,000–80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary.

formulas.name: Menstrual cycle phases
formulas.formula: menstrual (days 1–5: endometrium breaks down);  follicular/proliferative (FSH, LH ↑; follicle grows, oestrogen rebuilds endometrium);  ovulation (~day 14: LH surge);  luteal/secretory (corpus luteum makes progesterone)

formulas.name: LH surge
formulas.formula: peak LH (and FSH) in mid-cycle → rupture of Graafian follicle → ovulation

formulas.name: Fertilisation
formulas.formula: in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube;  sperm contact zona pellucida → blocks entry of other sperm;  completes meiosis II of the secondary oocyte

formulas.name: Sex determination
formulas.formula: ovum always X;  sperm X or Y (50:50);  XX → female, XY → male
formulas.note: The father's sperm decides the sex of the baby.

formulas.name: Early development
formulas.formula: zygote → cleavage → morula (8–16 cells) → blastocyst (trophoblast outside, inner cell mass inside) → implantation in endometrium

formulas.name: Pregnancy hormones
formulas.formula: placenta: hCG, hPL, oestrogens, progestogens;  ovary in late pregnancy: relaxin

formulas.name: Parturition and lactation
formulas.formula: foetal ejection reflex → oxytocin from posterior pituitary → strong uterine contractions;  colostrum (first milk) has IgA antibodies

examples.title: Gamete output
examples.problem: How many sperm and ova form from one primary spermatocyte and one primary oocyte?
examples.solution: 4 sperm from one primary spermatocyte; 1 ovum (plus polar bodies) from one primary oocyte.

examples.title: Chromosomes in a spermatid
examples.problem: A human spermatogonium has 46 chromosomes. How many does a spermatid have?

examples.title: Corpus luteum
examples.problem: What happens to the corpus luteum if fertilisation does not occur?
examples.solution: It degenerates, progesterone falls, the endometrium breaks down and menstruation starts.

examples.title: Pregnancy test
examples.problem: Which hormone is detected in a pregnancy test kit?
examples.solution: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), made by the placenta (trophoblast) — present only during pregnancy.

examples.title: Organ development timeline
examples.problem: When does the foetal heartbeat start and when are limbs formed?
examples.solution: Heart forms after one month of pregnancy; by the end of the second month limbs and digits develop; by the end of 12 weeks (first trimester) most major organs have formed.

examples.title: Identical twins
examples.solution: A single zygote (or early embryo) splits into two, so both twins have the same genetic makeup. Fraternal twins come from two different eggs fertilised by two sperm.

topics.title: Female reproductive system
topics.explain: Ovaries (2–4 cm long) with stroma; oviducts with infundibulum (fimbriae collect the ovum), ampulla and isthmus; uterus with perimetrium, myometrium (smooth muscle; strong contractions at birth) and endometrium (glandular; cyclic changes); cervix and vagina. External genitalia: mons pubis, labia majora and minora, hymen, clitoris.

topics.title: Mammary glands
topics.explain: Paired, containing glandular tissue and fat. Each breast has 15–20 mammary lobes with alveoli that secrete milk; milk passes through tubules, ducts, ampulla and lactiferous duct to the nipple.

topics.title: Placenta
topics.explain: Formed by chorionic villi (from trophoblast) and uterine tissue, it supplies O₂ and nutrients to the embryo and removes CO₂ and wastes. It connects to the embryo by the umbilical cord and acts as an endocrine tissue.

topics.title: Germ layers
topics.explain: The inner cell mass forms ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm, which give rise to all tissues and organs. The inner cell mass contains stem cells that can form all tissues.

topics.title: Menarche and menopause
topics.explain: The first menstruation at puberty is menarche; cycles stop around 50 years of age (menopause). Cycles stop during pregnancy and can be irregular due to stress or poor health.

topics.title: Gestation
topics.explain: Human pregnancy lasts about 9 months. By the end of the second trimester the foetus has fine hair, eyelids separate and eyelashes form. The first foetal movements and hair on the head usually appear in the fifth month.

ratta: Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens.
1 primary spermatocyte → 4 sperm;  1 primary oocyte → 1 ovum.
Fertilisation in ampulla;  implantation as blastocyst.
hCG, hPL, relaxin — only in pregnancy.
Pregnancy: heart after 1 month;  limbs/digits by end of month 2;  major organs by 12 weeks;  movements + head hair in month 5;  body hair, eyelids, eyelashes by 24 weeks.
